picks.excerpt: OpenAI's first hardware product is reportedly a portable, screenless 'AI companion' speaker: per Bloomberg it runs an advanced GPT-Live voice mode, has moving mechanical parts to feel 'alive,' and packs cameras and sensors for contextual awareness.
picks.rationale: OpenAI's debut hardware is the marquee gadget story; kept the strongest of four outlets covering it (original Bloomberg-sourced report, most complete).

picks.excerpt: After a year's delay, Apple's rebuilt Siri AI - now powered by Google's Gemini models - ships in iOS 27; a month of use finds it genuinely useful for searching personal data and multi-step tasks, though still short of flawless.
picks.rationale: Shipping-now, one-month verdict on the Gemini-powered Siri in iOS 27; actionable for anyone leaning on Apple's assistant, and distinct from the prior watchOS/visionOS beta-seeding notes.

picks.excerpt: Google's Gemma 4 E2B runs directly on the Pixel 10's Tensor G5 TPU, enabling on-device offline AI chat, image recognition and voice transcription with no internet connection - a push for local, private generative AI on the phone.
picks.rationale: Concrete on-device / offline generative AI on shipping hardware - a real shift toward local, private phone AI that changes how designers can rely on it.

picks.excerpt: Meta starts charging $20/month for Meta One Premium, gating the smart glasses' AI 'Conversation Focus' feature to just 3 hours/month free (15 hours paid) - a look at how on-device AI capabilities on wearables are being monetized.
picks.rationale: First clear signal of how AI wearable features get monetized; distinct topic (pricing/subscription) from the published Meta glasses privacy/super-sensing stories.
